title: Order state machines and idempotency
objectives: Separate local submit/cancel intent,venue event/status and filled/open/closed-unexecuted quantities under a narrow explicit order transition model,including fills during pending cancel.

Use source/order/epoch-bound normalized event identity for exact duplicate no-op versus content conflict,and explain why local projection idempotency does not provide durable exactly-once external execution.
Apply order state machines and idempotency invariants safely and identify scope boundaries.
motivation: A command asks for an action; an event reports a source-confirmed occurrence; a status summarizes state after relevant events. Sending an order is not venue acceptance, acceptance is not a fill, and requesting cancellation is not cancellation confirmation.

blocks.md: A command asks for an action; an event reports a source-confirmed occurrence; a status summarizes state after relevant events. Sending an order is not venue acceptance, acceptance is not a fill, and requesting cancellation is not cancellation confirmation. FIX ExecType(150) explains why an ExecutionReport was sent, while OrdStatus(39) describes reported state with precedence rules. Pending Cancel can take precedence over partial/filled states while the request is unresolved. A single status string without quantities/source identity can therefore mislead. Never zero possible exposure solely because a cancel request was sent.

Our code is deliberately narrower than FIX: ONE fixed-quantity order, ONE trusted normalized order/epoch namespace, quantity 1..100 and <=32 input events. ACK moves submitted->working; REJECT is allowed only from submitted in this toy. FILL is allowed only after ACK while working, including while our local cancel flag is true. A full fill changes phase to filled. CANCEL_REQUEST sets a LOCAL pending flag while working; CANCEL_ACK while working/pending closes the unfilled remainder; CANCEL_REJECT clears the flag while working or filled. No replaces, fees/prices, unsolicited cancels, trade corrections/busts, multi-day rules or full FIX status precedence are implemented. Real FIX permits scenarios excluded here, including rejection after acknowledgement and some reduced-verbosity paths.

For this projection retain filled, remaining candidate quantity and unexecuted_closed. Required nonnegative accounting is quantity=filled+remaining+unexecuted_closed. Submitted quantity is conservatively a possible outstanding candidate, not proof of venue acceptance. On cancel/reject, remaining becomes 0 but previously filled quantity stays filled; closed unexecuted remainder is tracked separately. These are OWN fields, not a universal mapping to FIX LeavesQty. Canceled quantity is not a reversal of confirmed fills or an account cash refund.

blocks.title: A fill can cross a cancel request
items: Order 10 is ACKed; FILL 3 leaves filled 3, remaining 7. Send local CANCEL_REQUEST: flag true, but remaining 7 is still possible execution.
FILL 2 arrives before cancel confirmation: filled 5, remaining 5, flag still true. CANCEL_ACK then closes the 5 unfilled units: phase canceled, filled 5, remaining 0, unexecuted_closed 5.

Alternative: after cancel request, FILL 10 completes the entire order. The cancel can then be rejected as too late; phase remains filled and the local request flag clears. The model does not pretend the request prevented the fill.

blocks.caption: Expected first tuple: ('canceled', 5, 0, 5, False, (1,2,3,4,5)) with Python spacing; second line True; third ('filled',10,0,0,False,(1,2,3,4)); last conflicting event identity. Pure full-batch projection returns only after all validation/transitions succeed; on ValueError no candidate result is published and caller inputs are unchanged. It records accepted normalized event IDs only within this one supplied history, not a durable ID store or real command/execution ID assignment.

blocks.md: Each normalized event is (event_id, kind, amount); exact ID+tuple duplicate is a no-op, even if repeated after a terminal state. Same ID with different tuple raises conflict before any candidate can be returned. A fresh event ID is not a license for an otherwise invalid transition, and a mathematically identical FILL under a fresh ID would count again if permitted by remaining quantity. Actual identity must bind source/session/order/execution namespace, not a guessed timestamp or payload amount. This toy has one namespace by construction; a real multi-order engine needs those explicit keys and a declared retention policy. Do not deduplicate equal-size legitimate fills merely because their values match.

Idempotent local projection means replaying identical normalized history/duplicates gives the same local result. It does NOT mean a sent external order executes exactly once. A timeout after send may leave an unknown outcome; blind resend can create a second order unless the venue's client-ID/session rules and reconciliation establish what happened. Persisting accepted identity and applying a local transition together needs a transactional/concurrency/recovery protocol. This pure full-batch function has none of those external effects or durable guarantees. If a fresh invalid event fails, retain the prior valid history and investigate; do not silently advance sequence/mark it applied.

Review each transition guard and the quantity invariant after every valid prefix. Include duplicate fill no-op, conflicting ID, overfill, fill before ACK, fill after canceled/rejected, duplicate terminal event, fill during pending cancel, full fill then cancel reject and rejection with zero fills. A rejected transition returns no new candidate for that batch; no caller-owned list/dict is mutated. These tests verify the explicit toy model, not every legal real FIX/venue sequence. A production engine must represent additional source events/status precedence and reconcile open orders/executions before assigning current exposure.

Independent transfer: build a reference transition table and enumerate bounded event streams, checking quantity decomposition, phase/flag consistency and duplicate invariance. Use unique source-bound fill IDs and prove two distinct equal-size fills remain two events. Extend only after writing new scenarios: partial cancel/replace, execution correction and reconnect unknown outcome require changed semantics/tests, not a silent else branch accepting anything. Keep the reducer separate from any live-send adapter.

Sources: [FIX EP284 Order State Changes November 2023](https://www.fixtrading.org/wp-content/uploads/download-manager-files/FIX-Latest-as-of-EP284-Order-State-Changes.pdf), [versioned FIX order-state package](https://fixtrading.org/packages/fix-latest-specification-order-state-changes/), [FIX Session Layer June 2020 duplicate/resend identities](https://www.fixtrading.org/wp-content/uploads/download-manager-files/FIX_Session_Layer_June_2020.pdf), and [event-sourcing concurrency/idempotency tradeoffs](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/architecture/patterns/event-sourcing). The authored normalized model has its own smaller state graph/local flag, not the full FIX OrdStatus state machine or a live execution certification.

guidedExercise.prompt: Why is a duplicate map insufficient to guarantee an external order is sent/executed exactly once across crashes?
hints: Names crash/timeout unknown state and reconciliation.
Does not infer external exactly-once from projection deduplication.
guidedExercise.solution: The send, remote acceptance/execution and durable processed marker are different boundaries. Crash/timeout can leave unknown outcome; need venue-supported identity/session/retry rules, atomic local state/marker protocol,retention/concurrency handling and independent reconciliation. A local pure replay map cannot certify the external side effect or grant trading authority.

independentExercise.prompt: Write a small test case that deliberately breaks the contract boundary in "Order state machines and idempotency" and verify how your implementation rejects or handles it.
hints: Test zero, negative, empty, duplicate, and boundary values.
Confirm both time/memory complexity and numerical precision remain within spec.

commonMistakes: Cancel and execution can cross; do not treat local intent as confirmed state. (Preserve exposure until source events/reconciliation establish the outcome.)
Duplicate no-op requires agreement under the stated identity/content contract. (The source/order/epoch identity must agree with content.)
Remaining becomes 0 while filled stays 5 and unexecuted_closed=5.

summary: Intent, source events and reported order status differ.
Pending cancel does not remove fill exposure; preserve quantity accounting and source-bound event identity.
Exact local duplicate no-op is not durable exactly-once execution, full FIX compatibility or account reconciliation.

quiz.prompt: A cancel request was sent for a partly filled order. What can still happen before confirmation?
options: The unfilled remainder is guaranteed to vanish immediately
The earlier fills are automatically reversed
Additional fills can arrive while cancellation is pending
The pending flag prevents a later full fill from becoming terminal
quiz.explanation: Cancel and execution can cross; do not treat local intent as confirmed state. (Preserve exposure until source events/reconciliation establish the outcome.)

quiz.prompt: Under this normalized model, same event ID with different tuple content means what?
options: Conflict, error and no new batch candidate
Always apply it as a new fill
A guarantee a venue has executed exactly once
quiz.explanation: Duplicate no-op requires agreement under the stated identity/content contract. (The source/order/epoch identity must agree with content.)

quiz.prompt: Order quantity 10 has filled 5 and a confirmed cancel closes all remaining 5. What remaining candidate quantity does this model report?
quiz.explanation: Remaining becomes 0 while filled stays 5 and unexecuted_closed=5.

quiz.prompt: How do FIX ExecType and OrdStatus differ?
options: Event reason versus reported state with precedence
Both are always a filled quantity in cents
Both prove a cancellation was successful whenever pending
OrdStatus always equals the most recent ExecType even when states overlap
quiz.explanation: Do not confuse the reason for a report with all underlying state dimensions. (One status label need not reveal all quantity/request dimensions.)

quiz.prompt: Two legitimate equal-size fills have different source-bound execution IDs. Should equal amounts alone deduplicate them?
options: Yes, every repeated amount is a duplicate
Yes, if it makes PnL smaller
Only if the UI needs fewer rows
No; identity is not merely payload size
quiz.explanation: Avoid merging distinct events just because values happen to match. (Each real execution needs its own bound identity.)
